entities.summary: Robert Murray Keith was a British diplomat of Scottish descent, born into a younger son of the 2nd Earl Marischal. He served as the British Ambassador to the Netherlands from 1769 to 1774, navigating the complexities of pre-revolutionary Dutch politics. Keith's tenure was marked by his efforts to prevent the Dutch from aligning with the French, despite being outnumbered and outgunned by the French forces in the Netherlands. He successfully maintained British neutrality during the Seven Years' War, earning recognition from the British government for his diplomatic skills. Keith's legacy lies in his contribution to British foreign policy during a pivotal moment in European history, as he skillfully navigated the treacherous landscape of pre-revolutionary Europe. The quote 'I am not a politician, I am a diplomat,' attributed to Keith, encapsulates his pragmatic approach to international relations. Keith's diplomatic career demonstrates the enduring importance of effective communication and strategic maneuvering in the pursuit of national interests.
